Traditional history frames Native Americans as
tragic victims of European colonial expansion.
The Reality
In his Bancroft Prize-winning work, historian Pekka
Hämäläinen shatters this assumption. During the
18th and early 19th centuries, the Comanches were
not passive subjects-they were a supreme imperial
power that surpassed European rivals in military
strength, political influence, and economic activity.

The Shape of Power
The Comanche Empire forces a complete reevaluation of
North American history. They were not victims swept aside by the
inevitable march of European progress. For over a century,
through a brilliant synthesis of equestrian mastery,
ecological dominance, and calculated diplomacy, they built an
indigenous empire that dictated the terms of survival to the
world's greatest colonial powers.
The story of the American Southwest is not just a story of
European conquest, but of unparalleled indigenous sovereignty.
